units.function: Unit test aggregating quota-window reports from all registered server adapters while timing out a provider that never resolves.
units.dependencyDirection: Global Adapter registry exposes optional quota pollers; an aggregation service executes them and returns provider-specific success or timeout projections.
units.keyDataModels: Adapter type, provider/source/ok/error, quota window label/usedPercent/resetsAt/valueLabel/detail and fixed 20-second timeout.
units.lifecycle: A responsive Codex poll returns its window; a never-resolving Claude poll becomes a synthetic Anthropic failure after 20 seconds without preventing aggregate completion.
units.testAssessment: Fake timers prove one hung provider cannot block forever. Missing are cancellation/AbortSignal of the underlying call, exceptions/malformed values, parallel timing, provider identity from capability declarations, configurable deadlines, stable error codes, stale-cache fallback, partial telemetry and resource-leak tests.
units.designRationale: Keep multi-provider quota UI available when one local vendor CLI hangs.
units.companyOsProblem: Agent Boss needs nonblocking, vendor-neutral cost/quota health but cannot confuse display estimates with enforceable Company budgets.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT bounded parallel capability polling with cancellation, stable health codes and observed-at/staleness. Keep provider quota telemetry separate from Company BudgetPolicy enforcement and cost evidence.
units.responsibilityConflict: A timeout string and vendor estimate do not authorize spending or prove cost. The hung operation is not cancelled, so it may continue using resources after the control plane reports failure.
evidence: 73eb2373 docs: use structured agent mentions in paperclip skill (#4103)

units.function: Unit tests building Project-indexed task-count and positive-budget maps for list projections.
units.dependencyDirection: Aggregated database rows enter a pure projection helper; null Project task rows are dropped and positive budget policies become display metadata.
units.keyDataModels: Project/scope ID, task count, budget amount cents, calendar-month/lifetime window and two Maps.
units.lifecycle: Counts map by Project, null IDs are ignored; positive budgets surface with window kind, while zero and negative values disappear as if unset.
units.testAssessment: Basic mapping branches are covered, but the test claiming string coercion passes a runtime number cast through TypeScript and therefore does not test string input. Missing are NaN/overflow/decimal/currency, duplicate rows, zero-as-hard-stop semantics, explicit unlimited/unset states and policy version/effective dates.
units.designRationale: Provide compact Project-list metrics and avoid displaying nonsensical nonpositive configured budgets.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must distinguish absent, unlimited, hard-zero, exhausted and invalid budgets because they change whether Agent work may execute.
units.companyOsFit: Reject omission semantics. Define an explicit BudgetPolicy state machine with currency/window/source/version and preserve zero as a valid hard stop; invalid negative values fail validation. UI projection consumes policy state rather than inferring it from positivity.
units.responsibilityConflict: Dropping zero can visually and operationally erase an intentional no-spend decision. Projection lacks who set the budget, when it became effective and which Work/cost owner it controls.
evidence: eaef47f4 Information Architecture + project/agent visual refresh (experimental) (#7543)

units.function: Embedded-Postgres HTTP regression tests normalizing single, CSV, repeated and mixed Issue status query parameters.
units.dependencyDirection: Board-authenticated Express query shapes enter Issue routes, normalize to status filters and execute against real Company-scoped database rows.
units.keyDataModels: Company/Issue status and query string/array/CSV shapes.
units.lifecycle: Single and combined filters return matching statuses; absent filter returns all seeded statuses.
units.testAssessment: Real route/database behavior covers Express parser shape variation well. Missing are invalid/empty/duplicate/oversized values, whitespace/case/encoding, authorization negatives, pagination interaction and stable schema-generated client behavior.
units.designRationale: Prevent repeated query keys from crashing the list route and support common client encoding styles.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS APIs need stable structured filtering across Web/FDE clients.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE robust multi-value parsing; prefer generated API schemas, bounded arrays and structured validation errors rather than permissive route-local coercion.
units.responsibilityConflict: Filtering is presentation behavior and must not substitute for Company authorization or evidence access policy.

units.function: Plugin SDK host-client tests allowing execution-workspace metadata reads only when the plugin declares the corresponding capability.
units.dependencyDirection: Plugin ID/capabilities and host services build RPC handlers; plugin request plus invocation Company scope is forwarded to executionWorkspaces service or rejected with a stable capability-denied code.
units.keyDataModels: Plugin ID, execution.workspaces.read capability, workspace/company/project/path/cwd/repo/ref/branch/provider metadata and invocationScope Company ID.
units.lifecycle: A capable plugin reads workspace metadata through the host; an undeclared capability is denied before service invocation.
units.testAssessment: Positive routing and fail-before-service denial are covered. Missing are mismatched request/invocation Company IDs, workspace ownership, path/metadata minimization, per-plugin grants beyond manifest declaration, revocation, invocation identity, audit, rate limits and malicious host-service responses.
units.designRationale: Expose narrow host capabilities to plugins through RPC instead of direct server/database access.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a canonical Plugin/Connector host boundary with least privilege and tenant-scoped invocation context.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT capability-gated host services and stable denial codes. Treat manifest declaration as a request, not authority: resolve it against installed-package trust, Company grant, Work/data contract and invocation scope; return opaque workspace handles instead of raw host paths where possible.
units.responsibilityConflict: A declared capability alone authorizes access in the test, and absolute cwd/path leaks host topology. No accountable human grant, data scope or access evidence is bound to the invocation.
evidence: c6d4ee10 test: align current-master regression expectations (#9577)

units.function: Unit tests selecting and formatting the Paperclip API URL injected into local Agent environments.
units.dependencyDirection: Ambient runtime/API/listen Host and Port environment variables plus Agent/Company identity enter an Adapter utility that returns Paperclip-specific process environment.
units.lifecycle: Explicit runtime URL wins, then general API URL, then listen host/port; wildcard bind becomes localhost and IPv6 is bracketed.
units.testAssessment: Precedence, wildcard fallback and IPv6 formatting are covered. Missing are URL validation/schemes/credentials, malformed ports, external versus container reachability, trusted origin/SSRF, scoped bridge token injection/redaction and deployment-profile separation.
units.designRationale: Give Agent subprocesses a reachable callback endpoint across local, SSH and LAN arrangements.
units.companyOsProblem: Connector nodes need a scoped callback/queue endpoint without ambient vendor URLs or control-plane credentials becoming core runtime assumptions.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE address precedence only. Company OS execution receives an explicit ConnectorRuntimeContext with validated endpoint, short-lived audience-scoped token and network policy from the deployment adapter; never infer identity/security boundaries from ambient environment variables.
units.responsibilityConflict: The chosen URL is not bound to a deployment/Work attestation and may redirect Agent-originated data to an unintended endpoint if environment is altered.
